name: Singapore
prevalence_note: Singapore 2025-2026 warnings: government Officials Impersonation Scam; fake Friend Lost Phone Urgent Transfer Scam; tech Support Compromised Device Remote Access Scam; investment Learning Community and Stock Mentor Scam.
cross_border_note: Many calls come from abroad in English or Mandarin with spoofed local numbers.

scams.name: Government Officials Impersonation Scam
scams.signals_en: The caller claims to be from a local bank, police force, or financial regulator, accusing the recipient of involvement in money laundering or identity misuse.
scams.legit_en: Singapore government officials never ask members of the public to transfer money over a phone call, disclose banking or national digital identity credentials, install unofficial apps, or transfer calls directly to police.
bait_tactics: Sorry ah, I'm on the underground train right now and the line keeps cutting off—can you repeat your department name slowly?
Hold on, my bank account has the money lock feature turned on so I cannot transfer anything by phone anyway; let me check at the branch later.
I don't have my identity card with me right now, maybe I call back through the official government hotline when I reach home?

scams.name: Fake Friend Call Scam
scams.name_en: Fake Friend Lost Phone Urgent Transfer Scam
scams.signals_en: An unknown caller warmly asks if the recipient recognizes their voice, claiming they lost their mobile phone and switched numbers.
scams.legit_en: Real friends, relatives, and business contacts should always be verified by calling their previously saved phone number directly or meeting in person, and they will not demand urgent transfers to unfamiliar third-party bank accounts.
bait_tactics: Wait ah, your voice sounds quite different today—which primary school or office did we know each other from?
My daily transfer limit is set super low and my token is at home, so I really cannot send anything right now.

scams.name: Tech Support Remote Access Scam
scams.name_en: Tech Support Compromised Device Remote Access Scam
scams.signals_en: Posing as software or security helpdesk staff, the caller claims the recipient's computer or phone has been hacked or infected with malware.
scams.legit_en: Reputable technology companies and banks never make unsolicited calls offering virus removal, never ask users to install remote-control software, and never ask customers to approve banking token prompts during support calls.
bait_tactics: Oh, this laptop belongs to my company IT department and blocks all downloads without an administrator password.
My home broadband just dropped connection so the browser won't load anything—let me bring the device to the service centre tomorrow.
Why would fixing a computer virus need me to open my bank app? Wait ah, let me ask my nephew who works in IT first.

scams.name: Investment Chat Group Mentor Scam
scams.name_en: Investment Learning Community and Stock Mentor Scam
scams.signals_en: Following up on online ads or unsolicited outreach, the caller claims to represent a renowned university seminar or brokerage mentor group offering free stock tips.
scams.legit_en: Licensed financial institutions in Singapore are regulated on official directories, never guarantee risk-free investment returns over unsolicited calls or chat groups, and never ask clients to wire funds to personal accounts.
bait_tactics: Sounds interesting, can you give me your representative licence number first so I can look it up on the official regulator register?
I'm outside having lunch now and don't click links from unknown numbers—just mail your prospectus to my office.
All my savings are tied up in fixed deposits right now, so I have zero spare cash to open any new trading account.
